description: Ohio HB 6 successor provisions (HB 96/SB 52) gave county commissioners veto power over large wind and solar siting decisions, previously handled exclusively by the Ohio Power Siting Board. Materially shifts approval authority to local governments and has resulted in numerous project rejections.
Cooke County Commissioners Court voted to ban wind energy facilities in the unincorporated county through a resolution citing aesthetics, property values, and wildlife concerns.
Kentucky SB 4 (2024) imposed new setback and decommissioning bond requirements for solar facilities, and allowed counties to opt out of hosting utility-scale solar under certain conditions.

Proposed 124 MW wind project in Herkimer County faced sustained local opposition including petitions with thousands of signatures and repeated town board hearings. Developer withdrew application in 2023.

One of the largest proposed solar farms in the US (~1,500 MW, Benton/Tippecanoe counties) drew organized local opposition over farmland conversion and drainage. Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission approved it after extended hearings.

Local residents filed suit in Mason County Circuit Court challenging the Michigan Public Service Commission's approval of a Consumers Energy wind project, alleging inadequate environmental review and setback violations.
Coalition of commercial fishing interests appealed Virginia State Corporation Commission approval of Dominion Energy's CVOW project. Virginia Court of Appeals upheld the SCC order in 2024.
